item.title: GTA 6 will launch on PC just a few months after consoles, according to a new report.
item.description:
Rockstar reportedly plans to release GTA 6 on PC during the first quarter of 2027.
GamesBeat reported the news based on four sources who asked to remain anonymous. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two are yet to comment.
If true, it would mean GTA 6 hitting PC just a few months after it launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Some had anticipated a longer wait for the game on PC, given it took nearly two years for GTA 5 to launch on PC after consoles.
The PC launch may tie into the release of GTA 6's multiplayer mode, which fans are calling GTA Online 2 while they wait for official word from Rockstar. While Rockstar has yet to confirm an online mode for GTA 6, last month Twitch boss Dan Clancy said GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — will launch next year.
Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has always responded with vague comments when asked about the prospect of launching GTA 6 on PC, pointing to Rockstar for announcements. In May, Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that you're judged by serving the core. Like really serving the core consumer. If your core consumer isn't there, if they're not served first and best, you kind of don't hit your other consumers.”
Red Dead Redemption, GTA 5, LA Noire, Max Payne 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2 all came to PC after consoles. And while GTA's core audience may be on console, it has a huge fanbase of active players on PC, fueled by GTA Online and role-play servers.
Indeed, 12 months ago, Zelnick said the industry was “moving towards PC,” telling CNBC’s Squawk Box that the video game business was trending towards “open rather than closed.”
In 2024, Zelnick was asked if the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 was set in stone. Here’s his response in full:
Well, the lack of an announcement is not something that could be set in stone as near as I could tell, because the only thing that happens after the lack of an announcement is an announcement, I suppose, or a continuing lack of an announcement, I guess that could happen too. It doesn’t seem to me that either would be set in stone.
But Rockstar has an approach to platforms which we’ve seen before, and they will make more announcements in due time. I do believe that the right strategy for our business is to be where the consumer is, and historically what this company has done is address consumers anywhere they are, on any platform that makes sense, over time.
Assuming GTA 6 does come to PC early next year, one of the big questions players will have is how it runs compared to on consoles. Rockstar has yet to confirm the performance of GTA 6 on consoles, so we're still in the dark when it comes to frames-per-second and resolution. But the expectation is that any PC version would be capable of better performance, assuming your rig is powerful enough.
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: 25 years later, Dan Houser recalls how GTA’s iconic cover art style only exists because of 9/11.
item.description:
There’s arguably no more recognisable style of cover art than that of the Grand Theft Auto series. The panelled collection of images featuring characters and locations from each open world that has adorned each game box from 2001’s GTA 3 to the upcoming GTA 6 is etched into each of our minds. It all nearly looked completely different, though.
We spoke to Dan Houser, former VP at Rockstar and writer of almost all of the studio’s games from 1999 until 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. When reminiscing about the developer’s most famous series, Grand Theft Auto, Houser shared how it felt to see elements of his creation permeate into the real world.
“GTA has become part of the wider cultural fabric,” he said. “I mean, you sort of saw that on YouTube clips and whatever else that would have the HUD on it, and people using the logo and things like that. When you go to any big tourist resort, you'll have a sort of GTA cover art-inspired T-shirt available. So you began to see that creep in 10 years ago, so I suppose.”
The bold, colourful style of that cover art came out of tragedy, though, as Houser revealed that the original look for GTA 3’s box had to be changed at the last minute due to the New York terror attack on September 11, 2011.
“What's funny is the cover art that became the iconic GTA cover art; Stephen Bliss did that in about two evenings because the old cover art was probably being too offensive to release after 9/11 because they were burning buildings in it,” Houser revealed. “So it would've been fine if there hadn't just been 9/11. So that look of the shards, the squares that became very iconic, only appeared because of 9/11.”
These changes, as well as some involving the actual content of the game, meant a slight delay for GTA 3 from its originally planned release date of October 3, 2001 to October 22. Though only a few weeks, it piled on the pressure for Rockstar and Houser, who were by no means sure it would become the landmark success it eventually did.
“So I remember in early 2001, Take-Two was on the point of economic failure at the time,” Houser recalled. “We were struggling to get the game done, but we thought the game was going to be amazing and took it to E3 on the show floor and nobody cared about it. So that was dispiriting up to a point. And then the game came out six, seven months later. And that was just after 9/11.”
GTA 3, of course, takes place in Liberty City, a fictionalised version of New York City, so you can see why a change in approach was needed. “There were a couple of bits of content that would've been fine, but in the exact aftermath of 9/11, were maybe a little bit too much,” Houser explained. “So we had to take those out, and the team will rally round and remove those and edit a couple of lines of dialogue and did a quick content stand and thought it was fine. And then the game came out in October of 2001. It kind of was a gradual all the way through till Christmas 2001 into early 2002, and it just didn't stop selling. It's not like any single week was that massive. It was that every week it just rumbled on.”
Some of these tweaks were detailed by Houser in a 2011 interview with Edge magazine. "As far as I recall, we changed the colour of the cop cars so they weren't identical to NYPD, we altered the flight path of a plane so that it didn't look like it was flying into or behind a skyscraper, and we removed one mission as it made a reference to terrorists,” he said at the time.
The first 3D Grand Theft Auto wasn’t the only piece of media that had to make alterations in the wake of the terror attacks. Other video games, such as EA’s Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2, had to redesign its packaging, and Hideo Kojima’s Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty had sections involving the destruction of parts of Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty removed.
Other cases include the trailer for Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man having to be recut to remove a helicopter being caught in a giant web between the World Trade Center towers. Men in Black 2 underwent huge reshoots for similar reasons, and planned sequels to both True Lies and Forrest Gump were cancelled.
25 years on, the same template for GTA game covers is still being used. You can check out all of the details we picked out from GTA 6’s art reveal here. For more on GTA 6, you can read our full interview with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson, how the game will tackle the current political climate, and why Dan Houser says he won’t be playing it.
Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social.

item.title: 20 years later, Dan Houser reveals how intense controversy made Bully one of Rockstar’s toughest games to make.
item.description:
Rockstar is gearing up for the launch of GTA 6, but, of course, Grand Theft Auto isn’t the only series the developer is known for. Alongside the likes of the beloved Red Dead Redemption games, there are many fans of another open-world adventure from the studio: Bully.
Released in 2006 and originally known in Europe as Canis Canem Edit, Bully tells the story of unruly student Jimmy Hopkins getting in and out of trouble during a year at Bullworth Academy. A smaller-scale, less X-rated version of GTA, it launched to critical acclaim. But the road towards launch was far from easy.
“The development was hard,” former Rockstar VP and writer of Bully, Dan Houser, said in a new interview as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. “The game was in trouble all of the time. It was difficult. It was an out-there concept. We were struggling with it. I wasn't sure it was going to be any good. We really wanted it to come together. It was really fun afterwards because it came together really well. The team did a great job. It was a sort of really strong game at the end. It kind of came together very late.”
Houser went on to explain why the development of Bully proved such a challenge, coming as it did just over a year after GTA: San Andreas. “New IP is very stressful because you're doing something that no one's ever done before,” he said. “And particularly that game, there was all of this controversy around it to do with the name, or people misunderstood it when they'd never seen it. So I think one of the challenges with that game was it never got the attention it deserved. We were too focused on trying to at least get people to stock it or to not protest it before it even came out.”
The mid-2000s was an era when controversy followed Rockstar games whenever one was about to hit store shelves, whether it be the snuff-film-fuelled ultraviolence of Manhunt, or the sex minigame mod, Hot Coffee, uncovered in the code of San Andreas. Bully was no different, with some members of the public worried about how its explicit content would translate into a school setting.
“There was huge hysteria around it,” Houser stated. “We had to spend most of 2006 diffusing it, so we couldn't positively promote the game in the way we normally would've done. I think that didn't help it. I mean, that was the same time as Hot Coffee, and it felt like things were imploding. It was very stressful. And just go to work each day, wonder who's protesting you that day, and hope that things can shake out properly. I wasn't directly involved. Luckily, I was just sort of right off to the side, and wasn't directly involved in organizing most of that stuff. But it was really stressful for the people involved.”
But it wasn’t just external pressures that made the development of Bully difficult. Rockstar also had to wrestle with how to make its style of open-world action-adventure work from the perspective of a teenager. The school setting meant driving cars and shooting guns had to be parked to one side — two vital gameplay mechanics of any GTA.
“Developers were struggling with what the IP was, and we'd made some changes, and some people had moved out there from New York, and it was starting to get a bit better, but it was still really struggling,” revealed Houser. “It was really, well, if you take away the cars and you take away the guns, what is the game? What are you doing? And the lead designer, who was really talented, began to put in the schedule and began to put in the lessons, and it was starting to get there.
“Then, one of the designers put this thing where you could stick a Post-it note on the back of a character that said ‘Kick me’ on it. Then an NPC would run up and kick them. And just seeing that work, you're like, that's a great moment. So then you're, okay, we're starting to get somewhere. So I think that moment was probably when I always remember going, this IP that wouldn't work in a GTA, obviously; it's not interesting. But as a kid, and suddenly it was the scale of the school and the scale of a kid's life, it started to feel really fun.”
Bully was indeed very fun. So much so that fans have been begging for a sequel ever since. While ideas for a follow-up were once floated around at Rockstar, Houser revealed to IGN in 2025 that it never got off the ground due to “bandwidth issues.”
I do miss the days when you’d get a new Rockstar open world to roam around in every year, but I guess at some point I have to give up yearning for the PS2 era. It was 20 years ago, after all. Luckily, Grand Theft Auto 6 is only weeks away from release.
For more on GTA 6, you can read our full interview with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson, how the game will tackle the current political climate, and why Dan Houser says he won’t be playing it.

item.title: Dan Houser was surprised ‘how angry some people were’ at Red Dead Redemption’s iconic ending, and reveals how the decision was made.
item.description:
Spoilers for Red Dead Redemption and Red Dead Redemption 2 follow.
The ending of 2010’s Red Dead Redemption is an all-timer. For dozens of hours, we’re placed in control of protagonist, John Marston, as he wanders across the American West in search of revenge against his former gang leader, Dutch Van der Linde. He, of course, gets it in a snowy showdown in one of its final missions. But John doesn’t get to live out his life in peace. That would be far too tidy an ending. Instead, the outlaw is gunned down by members of the army at his family farm’s barn.
It was a novel twist at the time. Open-world games, and games in general, didn’t do this. It initially split opinion, but has since gone down as a masterstroke in narrative design. Dan Houser, former VP of Rockstar and writer of Red Dead Redemption, recently spoke with IGN as part of our IGN30 Icons Series, and told us that it was just as difficult a decision to make as it sounds.
“I remember discussing it with the lead designer, Christian Cantamessa, and he was into it, and I was into it, but just knowing the production realities of… how does an open-world game work if you've killed the protagonist? So I said, ‘I think maybe we have to kill him.’ And he goes, ‘That's a great idea. Got to do it.’ I said, ‘I don't know if... let me just think about this,’ because we're just dealing with audio and dialogue. The nature of an open-world game is you finish a story, then you go back into the world and wrap up all the side content if you want to. We'd have to play as someone else for that. We could play as Jack, but what does that mean? So I had to think through for a while what it would mean production-wise.”
Jack is John’s son, and is only 16 years old for the majority of Red Dead Redemption’s runtime. For that transition of control to work, and for the game’s world to make sense, he’d need to become an adult, hence the three-year time jump to 1914 that sees us play as a 19-year-old Jack after his father’s death. But that was just one of the hurdles that faced Houser, Cantamessa, and the team at Rockstar.
“Did we have the skills and the bandwidth to play as Jack?” Houser recalled questioning. “Would it work? Technically, not story-wise. We'll figure out the story aspect. If you go and see a side character and they've got a three-mission arc and you've already done one mission, what would that actually mean if you came back? How would that work? We had to think through all of that stuff and concluded we could probably make it work, but we were still scared.”
The final story mission of the 2010 masterpiece sees Jack carry out his own act of cathartic revenge when he kills the person responsible for John’s murder in a duel. It’s the moment that makes it all work and ties the knot on the game’s story.
“I think people really loved that moment when you killed them and found it so powerful internally,” Houser said. “I think there was broad consensus that it was the right decision, but obviously it was an unusual and out-there decision, but I think the company had survived on making those decisions. I think we were surprised when the game came out by how angry some people were about that decision. There were people who were livid with you. And part of you goes, ‘That's fantastic,’ because it means you've really engaged in the story and the characters.
Another part was like, you forget, or I can forget sometimes, we're not making movies, we're not writing books, we're making games. The game can't live without a player. So they do feel ownership over what you and they are co-creating in the moment in a way someone looking at a painting, say, doesn't. And I think they felt really let down by this decision.
“Now, I think it was the right decision because you want those big, strong reactions, but I think people were really confused by it. As a writer, it was like he had to die for the story to have any weight, and I had wanted that in several GTAs. We’d never done it really for the technical reasons we just discussed.”
Houser seemingly enjoyed it so much that a similar trick was pulled in its sequel, Red Dead Redemption 2, this time arguably to even greater effect as the prequel bound us to Arthur Morgan before Marston once again took over the reins.
In a post-RDR2 world, Rockstar will once again be looking to push its storytelling capabilities forward in GTA 6 by letting us play as a couple on the run, Jason and Lucia. Will we still be able to play as both of them by the time the credits roll?
For more on GTA 6, you can read our full interview with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson, how the game will tackle the current political climate, and why Dan Houser says he won’t be playing it.

item.title: ‘I got that completely wrong’ — Dan Houser explains why he thinks Rockstar’s Max Payne 3 ‘failed’.
item.description:
Max Payne and its sequel, Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne, are two of the most genre-defining third-person shooters ever made. They propelled Finnish developer Remedy Entertainment into the spotlight as one of the most exciting studios making games. So, it was also going to be a challenge for another developer to pick up the third part of that trilogy. If you have the likes of Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption under your belt, though, you might just fancy your chances.
That’s what former Rockstar VP and writer of Max Payne 3, Dan Houser, thought, and while enjoying the process of making it, he now admits that it didn’t quite hit the mark. Despite being well-received critically, the 2012 game underperformed commercially, and wasn’t a huge hit with players. While Max Payne 3 is a great shooter in its own right, some questioned whether it tonally fit with its heavily noir-influenced predecessors, instead trading in the gloomy, introspective weirdness of Remedy’s New York set games for a more high-octane, colourful, all-action approach.
“It was a linear game, so it was a little different from writing an open-world game, a little more structured,” Houser told IGN as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. “I really enjoyed that as an experience. I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen. I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it.
“So I got that completely wrong,” Houser admitted. “I know Sam Lake [creator of Max Payne] well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success. The game is beautifully made, and it wasn't as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing.”
Max Payne 3 is certainly different in tone to what came before it, but I still hold a lot of love for it. Max Payne 2 remains one of my favourite games to this day due to the storytelling housed in its murky world, but there’s no denying that Rockstar brought something new and flashy to the table almost a decade later when taking the character to Brazil.
That bullet time still feels as sweet as ever to trigger, though, and if that level of polish can be brought over to Remedy’s upcoming remakes of the first two in the trilogy, then they can’t come soon enough. We last heard about the project over a year ago, when the studio revealed that it was in “full production” and that the "collaboration with Rockstar Games remains close and productive."
Of course, Rockstar currently has its plate very much full with the imminent launch of GTA 6 on November 19. item.title: Ben Affleck has compared the reaction to Tom Cruise’s Digger to “high-school bullying,” insisting the eagerness with which some have celebrated its box office failure could discourage risk-taking in Hollywood.
item.description:
Ben Affleck has compared the reaction to Tom Cruise’s Digger to “high-school bullying,” insisting the eagerness with which some have celebrated its box office failure could discourage risk-taking in Hollywood.
Digger is reportedly set to lose an eye-watering $250 million by the end of its theatrical run, with Warner Bros. expecting it to cap at around $40 million globally. Its opening weekend brought in just $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally. It's currently on $35.3 million globally after two weekends in theaters. Variety reported that Digger may go down one of the biggest Hollywood flops of all time.
Directed by back-to-back Best Director Oscar winner Alejandro G. Iñárritu (Birdman, The Revenant), and starring screen legend Tom Cruise, Digger has split both critics and audiences. Attempts have been made to weaponise the mixed reaction in its favour, and Hollywood stars have come out in its defence, but Digger does not appear to have the legs to recover from its initial box office disaster status.
Speaking on Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast, Batman star Ben Affleck defended ambitious filmmaking and risk-taking, issuing a warning that the reaction to Digger could see Hollywood retreat into safer bets such as sequels and recognizable IP adaptations.
"It's a little bit like the high-school bullying thing,” Affleck argued, “with people who hadn’t even seen movies. You see it happening now, frankly, with Digger. Everybody wants to celebrate this bomb as if it’s the most exciting thing to happen. And you think like, it’s a pretty ambitious, interesting movie made by interesting people who have talent.
“Everybody wants to count the money, what it lost or whatever. To me, I just think, if you punish movies that take risks, guess what you're going to get? A bunch of s**tty homogenized movies. You cannot do something interesting without taking a big swing. And that means you're going to sometimes look bad."
Digger has a 53% rating on Rotten Tomatoes' Tomatometer, and a more positive 74% user review rating on its Popcornmeter. IGN’s Digger review returned a 6/10. We said: “Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs.”
Digger trolled the negative reviews in its most recent ad campaign, but that failed to move the needle. Tom Cruise himself has yet to issue an official statement in response.

item.title: Everyone knows how seriously Marvel takes script security. The cast of 2015's Avengers Age of Ultron, for example, revealed that pages of the script had to be shredded every day on set to stop the plot leaking online. Marvel doesn’t email scripts, rather has a security guard hand deliver them. But what if an Avenger accidentally leaves their script on a plane?
item.description:
Everyone knows how seriously Marvel takes script security. The cast of 2015's Avengers Age of Ultron, for example, revealed that pages of the script had to be shredded every day on set to stop the plot leaking online. Marvel doesn’t email scripts, rather has a security guard hand deliver them. But what if an Avenger accidentally leaves their script on a plane?
That’s exactly what Paul Bettany, who plays Vision in new Disney+ show VisionQuest, did with the Avengers: Infinity War script. The British actor issued the shock revelation on Virgin Radio, and admitted having to tip a greeter $500 to get out of the hole he'd dug for himself
“I’ve never told anybody this, but I once left the entire script for Infinity War on a plane,” Bettany began, sparking a gasp from co-star Emily Hampshire, who plays E.D.I.T.H.
“And I got off the plane and I was in my car and I went, ‘Oh… oh… oh no!’
“And I was lucky to have had a greeter that was a genius, and I got the greeter to go in and get it. And I tipped that greeter like 500 bucks.”
That’s a lucky escape for Bettany, who risked spoiling one of the biggest Marvel movies of all time. That greeter certainly earnt their tip, forcing their way airside again to find that wayward script.
“They’re amazing,” Bettany said.
Hampshire, by the way, admitted losing a script for VisionQuest, saying security turned up at their house when they failed to return the sides (the scenes they’re to do that day). “Yes! I didn’t know they were precious. I probably threw them out!” she said.
The MCU is littered with examples of its actors spoiling key plot points. Ahead of the release of Age of Ultron, Scarlet Witch actor Elizabeth Olsen revealed an extreme security measure while filming. "It was quite funny that we had to burn our sides for the day... we weren't allowed to go home with our little pages of whatever we shot that day,” she told the BBC. "They took it from our trailers and shredded it. It's pretty crazy."
And, in a fun almost prophetic comment in the context of Bettany’s revelation, Olsen said at the time that Avengers should be watched on the big screen. "These films aren't plane movies... they deserve to be seen in a cinema the way it was made."
VisionQuest kicks off today, October 13, at 6pm PT / 9pm ET. Check out the revised VisionQuest release schedule here, and our spoiler-free review of VisionQuest Episodes 1 and 2 here.

item.title: Hideo Kojima posted pictures on social media of himself visiting Sony in Japan while wearing a Joy Division T-shirt — and fans are certainly getting plenty of joy out of it.
item.description:
Hideo Kojima posted pictures on social media of himself visiting Sony in Japan while wearing a Joy Division T-shirt — and fans are certainly getting plenty of joy out of it.
The Metal Gear creator took to social media to post the photos showing him standing outside Sony City, also known as the Sony Corporate Office Building, in Tokyo, Japan. That wouldn’t normally be anything to write home about, but given recent events, there’s plenty of context we need to run through.
Earlier this year, Sony ditched Physint, Kojima’s Metal Gear spiritual successor, leaving the legendary game developer scrambling to find another publisher for the project. In an interview with IGN, Kojima revealed how he feared for the future of Kojima Productions after Sony confirmed its decision via a Zoom call.
Visited Sony City. https://t.co/b1lUNSx5T0
Kojima pitched Physint to Microsoft and new gaming boss Asha Sharma, who were suitably impressed to snap up the cast adrift project, including its adaptation rights for film and TV. In the wake of Physint’s move to Xbox, Bloomberg reported that Sony had concerns around the success of Kojima’s Death Stranding, as well as Physint’s development timeline, budget, and platform strategy. Kojima Productions issued a statement in response, although it failed to directly address Bloomberg’s reporting.
“Make no mistake, this was a serious situation for the studio with a range of potentially significant implications,” Kojima Productions said. “While we recognise that the article may have caused alarm, we want to reassure you all, for the record: that the studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong.​”
In our interview, Kojima insisted there was no bad blood with Sony, saying: “... from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry. I've been working with them for like 30 years… Mr. Ken Kutaragi, Mr. Hirai, I was close with them. But it's not like that recently. I realized that, okay, this is the reality. It's the 10th anniversary of my studio. My studio might collapse, right?”
Kojima added that Sony did not provide a reason for canceling Physint, nor had it contacted him since the decision was made. “But I'm not fighting with Sony,” he continued. “We're not in a dispute. But what I want to say is that we've been together for 30 years and we have this relationship. So if this was the conclusion, I would've wanted to hear it a little earlier. But that meeting in June, they just gave us the final notice.
“As I said, my mind went blank, so I didn't really ask a lot of questions. It was more like, what should I do with my company? So that was what was on my mind at the time. I've always been a big Sony fan. I've been using a Walkman. All my cameras are Sony. So I have no bad feelings towards them.”
Fast forward four months, and we have Kojima visiting Sony. What should we make of this? Are the pair working on a secret project together? Could there be more to come from Death Stranding? Or is this… nothing? Either way, fans are having their fun, with people picking up on Kojima’s decision to wear a T-shirt for a band called Joy Division, and comparing the situation to Johnny Silverhand's ill-fated and destructive assault on Arasaka Tower in Cyberpunk 2077.
@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN https://t.co/GpmbAoq071
@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN https://t.co/4WiEYqAg3Z
@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN @Kojima_Hideo https://t.co/gpwQYTQc9n
After the Physint news broke, there has been intense speculation about the budget for the game. In a recent New York Times profile of Asha Sharma, it was reported that Xbox may have negotiated a deal for less than you’d expect for a full price, triple-A spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid from the creator of the franchise.
Kojima told IGN that Microsoft was “not thinking of just funding a game. They're thinking about movies and anime. It's more about the IP. Let's create a new IP. And that's bigger in scale, so to speak. And not many other game publishers or game developers have that kind of vision.”
Physint remains without a release window. It is expected after the launch of OD, Kojima's next video game for Xbox.

item.title: GTA 6 fans are celebrating after the Cyberleek memecoin crashed hard yesterday, scuppering the leaker’s crypto scheme.
item.description:
GTA 6 fans are celebrating after the Cyberleek memecoin crashed hard yesterday, scuppering the leaker’s crypto scheme.
Cyberleek had tied various types of GTA 6 gameplay leaks to the Cyberleek market cap, ranging from $5 million to $25 million. The leaker also threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200 GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap.
Already this week a number of gameplay clips were reportedly leaked after market cap goals were hit, including gameplay that allegedly shows Lucia fully naked, and, more recently, the alleged leak of a “Lucia closeup 4k” video.
Cyberleek has threatened to release a new unauthorized GTA 6 gameplay video every day, assuming the memecoin market cap targets were met, and launched yet another gameplay poll designed to encourage spending on the memecoin.
However, the Cyberleek memecoin has crashed, with a current market cap of $1.7 million, down from a high of $7.8 million on October 11. It is now highly unlikely to hit that $30 million target, and may struggle to hit the other targets Cyberleek had set for further leaks.
Of course, Cyberleek may ignore the targets and just release gameplay anyway. But the bigger question is whether Cyberleek really does have a build of GTA 6, and, if so, would actually release it. Assuming Cyberleek has a working build, releasing it into the wild would be catastrophic for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two, as it would no-doubt spark a frenzy of AI-powered projects that would threaten the potential success of GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S when it comes out next month.
For now, GTA 6 fans are celebrating the Cyberleek crash. “Whoever is dropping money on this deserves to lose their money lol. You are begging to get scammed,” one person said. “There is a god,” another added. “Anyone who gave this moron cash deserved this. What the hell did people expect?” another commented.
Fans had spent the last week calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and is likely to do so again ahead of GTA 6’s official release date, if they haven’t already. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.
Yesterday, IGN reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked. A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggests access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggests this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats and won’t be possible in the official release.
One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.
Cyberleek has threatened Rockstar and parent company Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they fail to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and, as we’ve explained, the market cap of the memecoin hits $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from a crypto scam.
"Here's the deal, nice and clean," Cyberleek's threat began. "CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out — full story mode, played to the end, credits and all. Don't believe it has full story mode? Ask for what you want to see, and it gets provided. Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing. Everyone knows which one they'll pick."
Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. But Cyberleek reemerged last week with the release of a 24-minute GTA 6 gameplay video that reportedly showed cutscenes, story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera.
It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. Recent developments suggest Cyberleek remains at large and defiant in the face of potential legal action.
In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.
Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible.

item.title: Mick Gordon Plans to Take His Upcoming Doom Concert Performance On the Road
item.description:
Award-winning composer and skull-shattering guitar shredder Mick Gordon has given an update on the scheduled live performances of his Doom and Doom Eternal soundtracks, explaining in an interview with IGN at PAX Australia this past weekend that his appearance as headliner at the UK’s RADAR festival in 2027 isn’t merely intended as a one-off.
“The two that we’ve announced are this headline show for RADAR, which is going to be on August 1, 2027,” said Gordon. “That’s going to be me with a band and a live orchestra playing music from Doom and Doom Eternal and some other stuff. Then a few days later I’m going to be in the Czech Republic playing the Brutal Assault Festival, which is in a medieval castle, which is so metal. That’s with bands like Children of Bodom, Knocked Loose, and Humanity's Last Breath. It's like a really, really incredible 25,000-people metal festival.”
That all sounds great, but what if you happen to be one of the millions of Doom fans that can’t make it to the UK or Europe in order to catch either of these two shows? Well, the good news is you might still get your chance to experience Mick’s heavy metal magnificence on a live stage near you sometime in the not too distant future.
“[After the RADAR show was announced] I instantly started getting offers from the European metal festival circuit,” said Gordon. “My agency and I are talking about doing this for the next two years. There are a number of [events] across the whole world that we’re hoping to take this show [to]. So there’s going to be a lot of news coming on that front.”
Gordon seems extremely excited to perform popular Doom tracks like Rip & Tear, BFG Division, and At Doom’s Gate in front of a live festival audience, and promises an experience unlike a typical concert performance of a videogame soundtrack.
“For a long time I’ve wanted to take what I find really exciting about videogame music and marry it with what I find really exciting about a live rock and metal show,” said Gordon. “I know there are people that have done [live performances] where [the audience] will sit down and wear nice clothes and listen to [their] favourite music played by an orchestra, and that’s fantastic, don’t get me wrong. But nobody has done this thing where you have this massive circle mosh pit with videogame music.”
“Through an incredible set of wonderful, universe-grifting circumstances, I found myself best positioned to be the one [to deliver that experience].”
In the meantime you can get a fresh dose of Gordon’s heavy metal mayhem on the soundtrack to Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2, which is out on October 14 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, with a Nintendo Switch 2 version coming at a later date.
Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. He has 25 years of experience covering video games, having served as Deputy Editor on Official PlayStation 2 Magazine Australia and as Editor of Official Xbox 360 Magazine Australia, before joining IGN in 2009. item.title: The first poster for Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is here, and it seems to have won over a few of the more skeptical fans.
item.description:
The first poster for Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is here, and it seems to have won over a few of the more skeptical fans.
Netflix shared an ethereal glimpse at the new Narnia movie on social media today. It came with the promise that a first look at the Barbie director's foray into the beloved fantasy universe will arrive via trailer tomorrow, though specifically when it will premiere is unclear.
The Narnia: The Magician's Nephew poster (below) seems to call back to art featured on some copies of author C. S. Lewis' original The Magician's Nephew novels. That would mean the three individuals illuminated by iridescent light here are Polly (Beatrice Campbell), Digory (David McKenna), and their flying horse, Fledge. The spacey lion gracing the background, meanwhile, teases Meryl Streep's Aslan.
The new poster for Gerwig's Netflix movie doesn't reveal much about its story or characters, but it's the look and feel that has fans taken aback. Even some of the more skeptical viewers, who have feared what an adaptation of Lewis' work would look like in 2026, like what they see here, with many taking to social media to praise the art.
"Well, that actually looks pretty awesome," one Reddit user said.
"Credit where credit is due, that is one hell of a poster," another added.
"It looks like a poster from a 1980s/early 1990s fantasy film and I am here for it," another user added.
That's not to say that there aren't still those who have yet to be impressed. Most of the concern seems to come from a place of dread that some of the most revered characters in fantasy could be warped or damaged on impact. Some naysayers are more vocal than others, but in reality, it's hard to say if Gerwig will land the plane just yet, but we'll definitely have a better idea when the film premieres next year.
"If I knew nooooothing else about this movie, I'd be excited," one of the more cautious fans said.
"I really like a lot of the visual stuff they’re doing with the movie," another explained. "Lots of cool filmic feeling stuff especially here. I just don’t like the time jump and the costume for Jadis doesn’t feel regal. It should be good technically but less so in other places."
In a relatively unlikely move from Netflix, Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is set to first come to theaters via IMAX sneak previews starting February 10, 2027. It will then receive a global wide release February 12, with streaming subscribers then able to watch from the comfort of their homes starting April 2.
Also included in the film's cast are Carey Mulligan, Daniel Craig, Emma Mackey, and Ciarán Hinds. While we wait to see how the movie may stray from the source material, you can check out more early details here. You can also check out what we learned after its logo reveal.

item.title: Nintendo was reportedly unhappy with Elon Musk's 2021 Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario.
item.description:
Nintendo was reportedly unhappy with Elon Musk's 2021 Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario.
In 2021, Elon Musk starred in a Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario. The nefarious Nintendo character took the stand in a courtroom, where he was being accused of murdering everyone's favorite plumber, Mario. The skit was poorly received online and, apparently, by Nintendo itself. Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang, two former Nintendo PR managers, revealed in a recent episode of their YouTube show that the SNL skit "did not go well" with Nintendo at the time.
The two got on the subject following the recent Saturday Night Live sketch where The Legend of Zelda protagonist Link and GTA 6's Jason Duvall debated each other over who would have the better game. The sketch largely pokes fun at The Legend of Zelda while trying to make GTA 6 seem like the "cooler" game, which itself led to some mixed reactions online. Nevertheless, Ellis and Yang think that it probably went over better than Musk's sketch.
The two recalled being at Nintendo when the skit aired and stated that it was "not beloved." Ellis went on to note that the sketch was also oddly timed, as there wasn't even a new Wario game or product when it happened. He went on to say that the sketch also pushed into "uncomfortable" for Nintendo, likely referencing some of the more risque jokes in the skit. The SNL crew made jokes about Mario using cocaine, Luigi sleeping with Princess Peach, and featured a video of Luigi's censored penis. It was... interesting, to say the least.
Naturally, it's understandable if Nintendo wasn't thrilled about its family-friendly characters being portrayed as sexual deviants. SNL has parodied Nintendo a number of other times, including a sketch featuring a dark and gritty version of Mario Kart, heavily inspired by HBO's adaptation of The Last of Us.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad, has died at 34.
item.description:
RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad, has died at 34.
TMZ reported that a county official in Texas confirmed the news that he died today, October 12, 2026. The site stated it was told that Mitte died by suicide.
Additional details surrounding his death are unclear. An investigation is ongoing.
Mitte started his career in Hollywood with a small role in Disney's Hannah Montana before appearing as the son of Bryan Cranston's Walter White when Breaking Bad premiered in 2008. He played Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. for 56 episodes, cementing him not only as one of the AMC show's most prominent characters, but one of the more recognizable characters in TV history.
Mitte appeared in all five seasons of Breaking Bad but went on to have an acting career that saw him contribute to different mediums across the entertainment spectrum. In 2013, he showed up in a music video for Steel Panther's "Party Like Tomorrow Is The End of the World." In 2014, he appeared in nine episodes of the television series Switched at Birth.
While his time on TV screens saw him also play roles in things like Now Apocalypse and This Close, his movie resume included parts in things like 2021's Triumph, 2020's The Oak Room, and 2019's All the Little Things We Kill. His most recent project saw him star as Joshua in this year's Talking to Stranger.
Representatives for Mitte shared a statement with TMZ confirming the passing. They called him a "beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate."
"RJ Mitte was best known for his role as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. on AMC’s critically acclaimed, award-winning series Breaking Bad," the message continued. "Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion. Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s."
Fans of Mitte's work have already taken to social media to share their condolences. Others are taking the time to remember his impact not only as an actor but also as an important disability rights advocate.
If you or someone you know is thinking of suicide, please call the 24/7 National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

item.title: As part of IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, we are proud to reveal five brand-new screenshots of For the Stars, Snail Games USA's upcoming space sandbox survival game that will have you exploring and settling planets, uncovering the secrets of alien civilizations, and much more.
item.description:
As part of IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, we are proud to reveal five brand-new screenshots of For the Stars, Snail Games USA's upcoming space sandbox survival game that will have you exploring and settling planets, uncovering the secrets of alien civilizations, and much more.
The images, which you can see below, show off some of For The Stars' different biomes, weapons, flora and fauna, vehicles, spaceships, and more. They also offer a glimpse into the multiplayer experience that allows friends to explore this universe together.
Players will be traveling from planet to planet and establishing outposts to upgrade their tech, studying alien artifacts and natural phenomena, and surviving any challenges that come their way in an effort to get more powerful and "explore further into the unknown."
Speaking of outposts, players will need to balance the needs of each area with proper laboratories, factories, and living quarters. Spacecraft will also need to be upgraded, and they can be customized to make them unique and suited for any task ahead.
And yes, friends can come along for the ride. Collaborate on building projects, share different discoveries, and work together to overcome any obstacle. Furthermore, Snail Games USA teases that players can "choose to enter contested regions to fight other players for control of the galaxy."
For more from IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, check out our main guide that explains how to watch, what to expect, and more.

item.title: A student at a Massachusetts middle school found herself at the center of a police investigation after administrators discovered her Death Note notebook.
item.description:
A student at a Massachusetts middle school found herself at the center of a police investigation after administrators discovered her Death Note notebook.
The incident took place at Chocksett Middle School in Sterling, Massachusetts. Students had already left for the day when staff discovered the notebook at around 4pm on September 30.
Police and school officials then conducted an investigation, interviewing both its owner and other students, and quickly determined that the Death Note — which contained a few names of its owner’s classmates — did not pose a legitimate threat. However, the student was suspended for three days.
“When we spoke with the student, the student explained that the notebook was connected to an anime television series and was not intended as a threat,” principal Tina Boss wrote in a letter addressed to the school’s community, adding that there was “no indication that the notebook or its contents were intended as a threat toward the school or any particular student.”
“Based on the information available at this time, the Sterling Police Department is not seeking criminal charges in connection with this incident,” the Sterling Police Department said in a press release.
Despite coming to this conclusion, police stood watch on the school grounds Tuesday, October 6, with officials saying it "will maintain a presence as it sees appropriate," as reported by local news outlet Boston.com.
A Death Note, in the anime of the same name, is a supernatural notebook owned by gods of death called shinigami. If someone writes the name of another person in the notebook, they will die. There are a few other rules, but that’s basically the gist of it.
Death Notes are often sold as merchandise for fans of the anime and manga series as basic notebooks with the 'Death Note' lettering on the front cover — but given the state of things in the United States over the last decade, it makes sense why parents and school administrators would be concerned for students’ safety after finding such a notebook. A mother of one of the children whose name was written in this particular Death Note expressed frustration with how the situation was handled on social media.
“A student who created a kill list with our daughter’s name on it is being allowed to return after just a three-day suspension… to the same classroom, within feet of her every day!” she wrote in a post on Facebook. “Yes, a safety plan is in place. But how does that plan give my daughter peace of mind when she still has to sit in the same classroom as the student who put her name on that list? She deserves to feel safe in her classroom, every single day.”
This isn’t the first time a student’s Death Note notebook has prompted such a reaction after being discovered at school; in September 2024, teachers at an I Promise school in Akron, Ohio were alerted after a student’s homemade ‘Death Note,’ written on sheets of loose leaf paper, was found. Although nothing came of the situation, parents of students whose names were written in the notebook similarly expressed dissatisfaction at how things were handled.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Epic Games has reportedly delayed its secret Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter as it pushes its developers to shift to an "AI first" production model.
item.description:
Epic Games has reportedly delayed its secret Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter as it pushes its developers to shift to an "AI first" production model.
Details on the yet-to-be-announced Disney video game were shared by Bloomberg today. The site's report stated the untitled crossover experience was slated for release in March, but has since been pushed back to accommodate a new internal release plan that has yet to be shared.
Epic developers attached to the project have reportedly been encouraged to use tools such as Anthropic's AI assistant, Claude, with humans expected to oversee that work. Bloomberg also obtained an internal message shared by one of the Star Wars/Marvel game's directors.
"No more hand-written code,” an excerpt from the message said. The same message is then said to have added that all art for the project would be "generated with full AI workflows."
The report continued, stating that Epic underestimated the time and resources necessary to develop the Star Wars and Marvel shooter. Progress has been slower than expected, leading to the delay. When and where it will launch is unclear.
"We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," Epic communications director Jake Jones told Bloomberg in a statement.
The site added that Epic's push for what appears to be a project that leans heavily on AI left many of its developers "stunned." News of the Star Wars and Marvel shooter's schedule change follows another Bloomberg report from earlier this year, which stated that Epic was working on an extraction shooter featuring Disney characters. It was said to be similar to Embark Studios' Arc Raiders at the time.
Just moments before news of Epic's AI push broke, studio founder and CEO Tim Sweeney published a post on X/Twitter saying that the studio has a "huge pivot underway." He added that they are "moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration."
"The aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people," he continued, "but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal." In a follow-up post, Sweeney said, "Our more modest aim is to survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster."
"The biggest change will be much faster time from having an idea to playtesting it," he said in another post. "This will be great for gameplay, as most of the recent AAA failures can be attributed to game systems going through far too much of their development process without being able to playtest."
Disney purchased a $1.5 billion stake in the Fortnite developer in 2024 in a move that cemented their relationship at the time. Outside of more crossovers within Epic's still-popular battle royale-centered video game, it seems we've yet to see the extent of their collaborations. Meanwhile, Disney recently refuted claims that it was interested in outright acquiring the game studio.

item.title: IGN can exclusively reveal Godzilla Versus Everything, a massive new crossover event that may well be IDW's most ambitious Godzilla comic ever.
item.description:
IDW has been busy establishing an ambitious new Godzilla line with the Kai-Sei Universe, which kicked off in 2025. Now, IGN can exclusively reveal that the Kai-Sei line will experience its first major crossover event in 2027.
The crossover in question is dubbed Godzilla Versus Everything. This four-issue miniseries sees Godzilla achieve his newest and most powerful form, forcing the casts of the flagship Godzilla comic, The Deadzone, Starship Godzilla, and The Horror of Godzilla to band together to save humanity.
Godzilla Versus Everything is written by Tim Seeley and illustrated by Fero Pe. Here's the official description for the series:
"When I started work with editor Jake Williams and IDW on GODZILLA, the big pitch was this was going to play like a universe of titles, but also as a universe of characters,” said Seeley in a statement. “From the beginning, the goal was they'd all come together at some point as friends and/or enemies in a proper comic universe event title. Well, we're here, and all the meticulous plotting of our creative crew leads to a wild, weird, terrifying crossover comic that puts Godzilla, the kaiju and our cast through every epic story beat you've ever wanted."
Godzilla Versus Everything #1 will debut in March 2027. Fans can also look forward to a lead-in to the crossover in March's Godzilla #17, which will be the final issue of the series. The buildup begins this month in Starship Godzilla: Invasion X #1, Godzilla: Revenge of the Deadzone #1, and Godzilla #13. You can preorder all of these comics at your local comic shop.
This isn't the only big news out of IDW. IGN also revealed that the publisher is kicking off "The Road to Sonic #100" in their ongoing Sonic the Hedgehog series. And at NYCC, IDW revealed that they've tapped Grant Morrison to write a new James Bond comic.

item.title: Marvel has published the full release schedule for VisionQuest, revealing an early premiere for Episode 1.
item.description:
Marvel has published the full release schedule for VisionQuest, revealing an early premiere for Episode 1.
The Vision (Paul Bettany) and Ultron-led (James Spader) Disney+ show's rollout plan materialized on Marvel Studios social media channels today – and it came with a bit of a surprise. Instead of starting its offshoot story on October 14 as originally planned, VisionQuest Episode 1 will arrive tomorrow, October 13, at 6pm PT / 9pm ET.
It's a one-day-early premiere that Marvel waited to announce until today, and it came with more specific information about the full release plan, too. Those hoping to keep up with VisionQuest can expect two episodes each week until its penultimate episode arrives alone November 3, with the eighth and final episode then arriving one week after that. You can see the full breakdown below.
Episode 1: "No Strings" and Episode 2: "Theseus" – October 13
Episode 3: "Reboot" and Episode 4: "Malware" – October 20
Episode 5: "Firewall" and Episode 6: "Deadlock" – October 27
Episode 7: "Immolation" – November 3
Episode 8: "Forever" – November 10
"Vision, rebooted and having escaped from those who sought to weaponize him, has been in hiding," an official synopsis for the show says. "Searching for new meaning, he consults the AI personas embedded in his programming, including Friday, Edith, Jarvis, and the infamous Ultron. His discreet existence ends when a bounty placed on his head thrusts him on the run with Thomas Shepard, a mysterious boy who may be Vision’s son, reincarnate."
VisionQuest will wrap up the WandaVision trilogy through the course of the next few weeks. It should provide a nice distraction as Marvel Cinematic Universe fans await the next big event film, Avengers: Doomsday, December 18, 2026.
The MCU will then gear up for a quiet year as it works to conclude the Multiverse Saga with Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027, but that doesn't mean there won't be anything to watch in the months between. While we wait to see how Vision's (mostly) standalone story will flesh out the universe, you can check out IGN's list of 10 streaming shows to keep an eye on in October. You can also check out everything we saw at the Marvel Television and Animation panel at New York Comic Con 2026.

item.title: A six-second video teaser posted to the official Beats by Dre YouTube channel shows the shadow of the Beats Pill speaker, enveloped by animated sparks and flames. The video, titled “Time to catch something new,” ends with an electrified Beats logo next to a Poké Ball.
item.description:
Beats by Dre has announced an upcoming collaboration with Pokémon.
A six-second video teaser posted to the official Beats by Dre YouTube channel shows the shadow of the Beats Pill speaker, enveloped by animated sparks and flames. The video, titled “Time to catch something new,” ends with an electrified Beats logo next to a Poké Ball.
The ‘electric’ animations suggest an unsurprising focus on the Pokémon mascot, Pikachu. To support that theory, unconfirmed images of a bright yellow Pikachu-themed speaker have already started circulating the web.
A full trailer was dropped within 24 hours, showing the real Pokémon edition speaker in its full glory, and revealing a second featured Pokémon, Mimikyu.
The Pokemon x Beats Pill will be available to purchase this Thursday, October 15, with a retail price of $149.99, the same as the standard model.
Pokémon is celebrating its 30th anniversary this year, giving the biggest franchise in the world the excuse to drop more collaborations than ever. We’ve seen themed hardware from tech companies like Razer, shoe drops from Crocs, and even entire merch collections with retailers like Target.
The amount of buzz going into the Pokémon brand right now would suggest any collab with the gaming giant is an easy win. However, an ongoing scalping crisis in the TCG market continues to bleed into all things Pokémon, with some commenters on the Beats by Dre teaser already deriding the collab as “The beats shill.”
Beats by Dre, which is owned by Apple, launched the first Beats Pill speaker back in 2012. The speaker has gone through a number of upgrades, most recently with a 2024 re-release focused on portability and power.
One thing that hasn't changed is the company's commitment to collaborations. Remember when the Beats Pill popped up in pretty much every YouTube channel? Nowadays, the company focuses on unique themed designs, having recently released product lines with Jennie (of Blackpink fame) and Kim Kardashian.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.
